<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Fixture test runner for Yggdrasil.

.DESCRIPTION
    Three fixture conventions are supported:
      *.jsx + *.expected.js   -- transpiler output must equal the .expected.js file
      *.jsx + *.expected_exit -- transpiler must exit with the code in that file (error tests)
      *.jsx + *.flags         -- extra CLI flags to pass to the transpiler (optional)

.PARAMETER Binary
    Path to the yggdrasil binary. Defaults to bin\yggdrasil.exe relative to repo root.

.PARAMETER Filter
    Optional glob filter on fixture base names, e.g. "01_*" or "err_*".
#>
param(
    [string]$Binary = "",
    [string]$Filter = "*"
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$RepoRoot    = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..") | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path
$FixturesDir = Join-Path $RepoRoot "tests\fixtures"

if ($Binary -eq "") {
    $Binary = Join-Path $RepoRoot "bin\yggdrasil.exe"
}

if (-not (Test-Path $Binary)) {
    Write-Error "Binary not found: $Binary`nBuild first with: .\build.ps1"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ANSI colour helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Green  { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Green  -NoNewline }
function Red    { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Red    -NoNewline }
function Yellow { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Yellow -NoNewline }
function Cyan   { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Cyan   -NoNewline }
function Nl     { Write-Host "" }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diff helper - show first divergence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Show-Diff {
    param([string]$Expected, [string]$Actual)
    $expLines = $Expected -split "`n"
    $actLines = $Actual   -split "`n"
    $max = [Math]::Max($expLines.Count, $actLines.Count)
    $shown = 0
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $max -and $shown -lt 8; $i++) {
        $e = if ($i -lt $expLines.Count) { $expLines[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
        $a = if ($i -lt $actLines.Count) { $actLines[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
        if ($e -ne $a) {
            Yellow "    line $($i+1):`n"; Nl
            Green  "      expected: $e"; Nl
            Red    "      actual  : $a"; Nl
            $shown++
        }
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collect fixtures
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$jsxFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $FixturesDir -Filter "$Filter.jsx" |
            Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^err_" -or $_.Name -match "^err_" } |
            Sort-Object Name

$pass = 0
$fail = 0
$skip = 0

Write-Host ""
Cyan "=== Yggdrasil Fixture Tests ==="; Nl
Write-Host "  Binary  : $Binary"
Write-Host "  Fixtures: $FixturesDir"
Write-Host "  Filter  : $Filter"
Write-Host ""

foreach ($jsx in $jsxFiles) {
    $base        = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($jsx.FullName)
    $expectedJs  = Join-Path $FixturesDir "$base.expected.js"
    $expectedExit= Join-Path $FixturesDir "$base.expected_exit"
    $flagsFile   = Join-Path $FixturesDir "$base.flags"

    # Read optional extra flags from .flags file
    $extraFlags = @()
    if (Test-Path $flagsFile) {
        $flagLine = (Get-Content $flagsFile -Raw).Trim()
        if ($flagLine -ne "") {
            # Split on whitespace respecting simple quoting is not needed here;
            # flags are space-separated CLI tokens with no embedded spaces.
            $extraFlags = $flagLine -split '\s+'
        }
    }

    # ---- Error-exit test ----
    if (Test-Path $expectedExit) {
        $wantExit = (Get-Content $expectedExit -Raw).Trim()
        # Build cmd line with optional extra flags
        $flagStr = if ($extraFlags.Count -gt 0) { ($extraFlags -join " ") + " " } else { "" }
        $null = cmd /c "`"$Binary`" $flagStr`"$($jsx.FullName)`"" "2>nul"
        $gotExit  = $LASTEXITCODE
        if ([string]$gotExit -eq $wantExit) {
            Green "  PASS"; Write-Host " [exit=$gotExit] $($jsx.Name)"
            $pass++
        } else {
            Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " [exit=$gotExit, want=$wantExit] $($jsx.Name)"
            $fail++
        }
        continue
    }

    # ---- Output comparison test ----
    if (-not (Test-Path $expectedJs)) {
        Yellow "  SKIP"; Write-Host " (no .expected.js) $($jsx.Name)"
        $skip++
        continue
    }

    $expected = (Get-Content $expectedJs -Raw).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd()
    try {
        if ($extraFlags.Count -gt 0) {
            $actual = (& $Binary @extraFlags $jsx.FullName 2>&1 | Out-String).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd()
        } else {
            $actual = (& $Binary $jsx.FullName 2>&1 | Out-String).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd()
        }
    } catch {
        $actual = ($_.ToString()).Replace("`r`n", "`n").TrimEnd()
    }
    $exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE

    if ($exitCode -ne 0) {
        Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " [exit=$exitCode] $($jsx.Name)"
        Write-Host "    stderr: $actual"
        $fail++
        continue
    }

    if ($actual -eq $expected) {
        Green "  PASS"; Write-Host " $($jsx.Name)"
        $pass++
    } else {
        Red   "  FAIL"; Write-Host " $($jsx.Name)"
        Show-Diff $expected $actual
        $fail++
    }
}

Write-Host ""
Cyan "Results: "; Nl
Green  "  $pass passed"; Nl
if ($fail -gt 0)  { Red    "  $fail failed"; Nl }
if ($skip -gt 0)  { Yellow "  $skip skipped"; Nl }
Write-Host ""

if ($fail -gt 0) { exit 1 } else { exit 0 }

arguments.content:
# Yggdrasil

A JSX-to-JavaScript transpiler written in C++17.  
Yggdrasil parses JSX source files and emits standard JavaScript — the same transformation Babel performs with `@babel/plugin-transform-react-jsx`.

---

## Features

### Stage 1 — Core JSX transpilation
- Self-closing, opening/closing, and nested JSX elements
- Component tags (uppercase), member-expression tags (`Foo.Bar`)
- String, expression, boolean, and spread (`{...obj}`) attributes
- JSX fragments (`<>...</>`)
- Text children, expression children (`{expr}`), and mapped children
- Full JavaScript support: `const`/`let`/`var`, arrow functions, destructuring, async/await, template literals, spread, ternary, logical operators, `import`/`export`
- Diagnostic output with line/column on parse and lex errors

### Stage 2 — Solid Tool extensions
- **Configurable JSX pragma** via `--pragma`: `react` (default), `h` (Preact/hyperscript), `jsx` (`_jsx`), or `auto` (React 17+ automatic runtime)
- **React 17 auto-import** injection: emits `import { jsx as _jsx, ... } from 'react/jsx-runtime'` when `--pragma auto`
- **Dev mode** (`--dev`): injects `__source` and `__self` props for React DevTools
- **Namespace tags**: `<svg:circle />`, `<math:mi />` → `"svg:circle"`
- **JSX comments**: `{/* ... */}` containers are silently dropped (no output)
- **Spread children**: `{...items}` inside JSX children → spread into `createElement` args
- **Hyphenated attributes**: `data-x`, `aria-label` → quoted keys in props object
- **Multi-error recovery** (`--recover`): collects up to 20 parse errors before aborting, reports all of them
- **Batch / directory mode**: `--out-dir <dir>` processes multiple files, writing `.js` output alongside
- **Nested ternaries in JSX**: fully supported
- **Complex attribute expressions**: arrow functions, block bodies, template literals, null-coalescing

---

## Building

### Requirements
- `clang++` (C++17)
- `make` (GNU Make)
- PowerShell 5.1+ (Windows) or bash (Unix/macOS)

### Build

```sh
# Default (debug-friendly)
make

# Optimised release
make release

# Debug with ASan/UBSan
make debug

# Clean
make clean
```

The binary is written to `bin/yggdrasil` (Unix) or `bin\yggdrasil.exe` (Windows).

---

## Usage

```
yggdrasil [options] <input.jsx> [<input2.jsx> ...]
yggdrasil [options] --out-dir <dir> <input.jsx> ...

Options:
  -o <file>        Write output to file (single-file mode)
  --out-dir <dir>  Output directory for batch mode
  --pragma <name>  JSX pragma: react (default), h, jsx, auto
  --dev            Emit __source/__self dev props
  --recover        Collect multiple errors instead of stopping on first
  -h, --help       Show this help
```

### Examples

```sh
# Basic transpile to stdout
yggdrasil App.jsx

# Write to file
yggdrasil App.jsx -o App.js

# Preact/hyperscript pragma
yggdrasil --pragma h App.jsx

# React 17 automatic runtime
yggdrasil --pragma auto App.jsx -o App.js

# Batch transpile a directory
yggdrasil --out-dir dist src/*.jsx

# Enable dev mode
yggdrasil --dev --pragma react App.jsx

# Recover from multiple errors (collect all, report together)
yggdrasil --recover App.jsx
```

---

## JSX Pragma Modes

| Flag | Pragma call | Fragment | Use case |
|------|-------------|----------|----------|
| `--pragma react` | `React.createElement` | `React.Fragment` | Classic React (default) |
| `--pragma h` | `h` | `Fragment` | Preact, hyperscript |
| `--pragma jsx` | `_jsx` | `_Fragment` | Custom runtime alias |
| `--pragma auto` | `_jsx` | `_Fragment` | React 17+ with auto-import |

`--pragma auto` prepends:
```js
import { jsx as _jsx, jsxs as _jsxs, Fragment as _Fragment } from "react/jsx-runtime";
```

---

## Running Tests

```sh
make test
```

Or directly with the PowerShell runner:

```powershell
powershell -File tests\runner\run_tests.ps1 -Binary bin\yggdrasil.exe

# Filter to specific fixtures
powershell -File tests\runner\run_tests.ps1 -Filter "3*"
```

### Test fixture conventions

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `*.jsx` | Input source |
| `*.expected.js` | Expected output (compared byte-for-byte after normalisation) |
| `*.expected_exit` | Expected exit code (for error tests) |
| `*.flags` | Optional extra CLI flags passed to the binary for that fixture |

---

## Architecture

```
include/
  token.h        TokenKind enum + Token struct
  lexer.h        Self-managing mode-stack lexer (JS / JSXTag / JSXChildren)
  ast.h          Flat Node struct + NodeKind enum (66 kinds)
  parser.h       Recursive-descent parser with JSX grammar branches
  codegen.h      CodeGen visitor + CodeGenOptions (pragma, dev, indent)
  diagnostics.h  LexError / ParseError / CodeGenError + ErrorCollector

src/
  lexer.cpp      Context-aware tokeniser; self-pushes/pops JSX modes
  parser.cpp     Full JS + JSX parser; optional multi-error recovery
  codegen.cpp    AST walker; lowers JSX to configurable pragma calls
  diagnostics.cpp ErrorCollector::dump() implementation
  main.cpp       CLI entry point; single-file and batch modes

tests/
  fixtures/      *.jsx + *.expected.js | *.expected_exit | *.flags
  runner/
    run_tests.ps1  PowerShell 5.1 fixture runner (cross-platform friendly)
```

### Key design decisions

**Self-managing lexer mode stack** — the lexer tracks JSX context internally (`JSXTag` / `JSXChildren` / `JS` modes), pushed/popped as it emits specific tokens. The parser never needs to call `pushMode`/`popMode` explicitly.

**Flat AST node** — all node kinds share one `Node` struct with named fields. Avoids virtual dispatch and header pollution from 66 separate node types.

**Raw-string destructuring** — parameter and variable destructuring patterns (`{ a, b }`, `[x, y]`) are stored as verbatim strings and re-emitted unchanged. This covers the MVP without full semantic analysis.

**Brace-depth tracking** — to correctly pop back from `{expr}` inside JSX, the lexer maintains a stack of brace depths. When the JS brace depth returns to the recorded value, the `}` is the container closer.

---

## Supported JSX Grammar

```
JSXElement ::= '<' JSXTagName JSXAttribute* ('/>' | '>' JSXChild* JSXClosingTag)
JSXFragment ::= '<>' JSXChild* '</>'
JSXTagName ::= Identifier ('.' Identifier)* | Identifier ':' Identifier
JSXChild ::= JSXText | JSXExprContainer | JSXElement | JSXFragment
JSXExprContainer ::= '{' ('...' Expr | Expr | /* JSX comment */) '}'
JSXAttribute ::= JSXSpread | JSXAttrName ('=' JSXAttrValue)?
JSXSpread ::= '{' '...' Expr '}'
JSXAttrName ::= Identifier ('-' Identifier)*   (e.g. data-x, aria-label)
JSXAttrValue ::= JSXString | JSXExprContainer
```

---

## Fixture Coverage (48 tests)

| Range | Coverage |
|-------|----------|
| 01–10 | Self-closing, open/close, text, string/expr/bool/spread attrs, expr child, nesting, fragments |
| 11–20 | Component/member tags, conditional `&&`, ternary, map, arrow component, multi-attr, deep nesting, multiple spreads, JSX in variable |
| 21–30 | JSX in array, fragment in return, plain JS, `<` as relational op, JSX in ternary, named imports + hooks, async component, null-coalesce/template attrs, sibling blocks |
| 31–44 | **Stage 2**: namespace tags, JSX comments, spread children, pragma h/jsx/auto, fragment with `h`, whitespace normalisation, adjacent JSX, complex attr expressions, aria attributes, multi-comment children, recover mode |
| err_01–04 | Mismatched tags, unclosed tag, bad attribute value, unexpected token |

Yggdrasil — Stage 3 Summary
Directory CLI & Batch Transpiler
What It Is
Yggdrasil shifts from single-file stdin/stdout to a directory-aware CLI tool. Point it at a source folder, get transpiled JS in a dist/ mirror. No module resolution, no bundling — still just a transpiler.
Core Features
Table
Feature	Description
Recursive directory scan	src/ → dist/ tree mirroring via std::filesystem
Batch transpilation	All .jsx files processed in parallel (thread pool)
Passthrough mode	Plain .js files copied untouched (optional --no-copy)
Watch mode	Re-transpile changed files on save (polling or OS-native watcher)
Extension rewrite	.jsx → .js in output; directory structure preserved
CLI Interface
plain
Copy

yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --watch
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --jsx-pragma h --no-copy --verbose

Table
Flag	Behavior
--out-dir <path>	Required for batch mode
--watch	Monitor source and re-transpile deltas
--jsx-pragma <name>	Override React.createElement
--jsx-runtime <classic|automatic>	React 17+ _jsx runtime vs classic
--no-copy	Skip non-JSX .js files
--verbose	Print src/components/Button.jsx → dist/components/Button.js
What Yggdrasil Stage 3 Does NOT Do

    ❌ Parse or resolve import/export
    ❌ Touch node_modules
    ❌ Build dependency graphs
    ❌ Bundle, concatenate, or tree-shake
    ❌ Handle CSS, assets, or non-JS files beyond copy/passthrough
    ❌ Source maps (already excluded by design)

C++ Implementation Notes

    std::filesystem::recursive_directory_iterator for scanning
    Thread pool (std::thread + std::queue + mutex) for parallel file processing
    Watch mode: simple polling loop (cross-platform) or OS-specific APIs (inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW) for efficiency
    Error isolation: one file failing doesn't kill the batch; aggregate error report at end

Output Example
plain
Copy

src/
  components/
    Button.jsx      →  dist/components/Button.js
    Icon.jsx        →  dist/components/Icon.js
  pages/
    Home.jsx        →  dist/pages/Home.js
  utils/
    helpers.js      →  dist/utils/helpers.js   (copied)

arguments.content:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Stage 3 batch/directory tests for Yggdrasil.

.DESCRIPTION
    Tests the directory-mode CLI:
      - Batch transpile src/ -> dist/   (recursive, parallel)
      - Passthrough: plain .js files copied untouched
      - --no-copy: plain .js files skipped
      - --pragma h / --jsx-pragma h: alt pragma in batch
      - --jsx-runtime automatic: same as --pragma auto
      - --verbose: prints per-file lines
      - --threads N: explicit thread count
      - Multiple explicit files with --out-dir
      - Error isolation: one bad file does not kill the batch

.PARAMETER Binary
    Path to the yggdrasil binary.
#>
param(
    [string]$Binary = ""
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$RepoRoot  = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..") | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path
$Stage3Dir = Join-Path $RepoRoot "tests\stage3"
$SrcDir    = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "src"
$ExpDir    = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "expected"

if ($Binary -eq "") {
    $Binary = Join-Path $RepoRoot "bin\yggdrasil.exe"
}
if (-not (Test-Path $Binary)) {
    Write-Error "Binary not found: $Binary"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Green  { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Green  -NoNewline }
function Red    { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Red    -NoNewline }
function Yellow { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Yellow -NoNewline }
function Cyan   { param($s) Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor Cyan   -NoNewline }
function Nl     { Write-Host "" }

$pass = 0
$fail = 0

function Assert-Pass { param($name)
    Green "  PASS"; Write-Host " $name"
    $script:pass++
}
function Assert-Fail { param($name, $reason)
    Red "  FAIL"; Write-Host " $name"
    Write-Host "    $reason"
    $script:fail++
}

function Compare-File {
    param([string]$Expected, [string]$Actual, [string]$Label)
    if (-not (Test-Path $Actual)) {
        Assert-Fail $Label "output file not created: $Actual"
        return $false
    }
    $exp = (Get-Content $Expected -Raw).Replace("`r`n","`n").TrimEnd()
    $act = (Get-Content $Actual   -Raw).Replace("`r`n","`n").TrimEnd()
    if ($exp -eq $act) {
        Assert-Pass $Label
        return $true
    } else {
        Assert-Fail $Label "content mismatch"
        $expL = $exp -split "`n"
        $actL = $act -split "`n"
        $max  = [Math]::Max($expL.Count, $actL.Count)
        $shown = 0
        for ($i = 0; $i -lt $max -and $shown -lt 4; $i++) {
            $e = if ($i -lt $expL.Count) { $expL[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
            $a = if ($i -lt $actL.Count) { $actL[$i] } else { "<missing>" }
            if ($e -ne $a) {
                Yellow "    line $($i+1):`n"; Nl
                Green  "      exp: $e"; Nl
                Red    "      act: $a"; Nl
                $shown++
            }
        }
        return $false
    }
}

function Remove-Dir { param($d)
    if (Test-Path $d) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $d }
}

Write-Host ""
Cyan "=== Yggdrasil Stage 3 Batch Tests ==="; Nl
Write-Host "  Binary : $Binary"
Write-Host "  SrcDir : $SrcDir"
Write-Host ""

# ===========================================================================
# Test 1: Basic directory batch  src/ -> dist1/
# ===========================================================================
$dist1 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist1"
Remove-Dir $dist1

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist1 2>&1 | Out-Null
$exit1 = $LASTEXITCODE

if ($exit1 -ne 0) {
    Assert-Fail "T1: batch exit code" "exited $exit1"
} else {
    Assert-Pass "T1: batch exit code 0"
}

Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "components\Button.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist1  "components\Button.js") `
             "T1: components/Button.js transpiled"

Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "components\Icon.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist1  "components\Icon.js") `
             "T1: components/Icon.js transpiled"

Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "pages\Home.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist1  "pages\Home.js") `
             "T1: pages/Home.js transpiled"

# Plain .js should be copied by default
Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "utils\helpers.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist1  "utils\helpers.js") `
             "T1: utils/helpers.js copied (passthrough)"

Remove-Dir $dist1

# ===========================================================================
# Test 2: --no-copy  (plain .js not copied)
# ===========================================================================
$dist2 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist2"
Remove-Dir $dist2

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist2 --no-copy 2>&1 | Out-Null

$helpersDst = Join-Path $dist2 "utils\helpers.js"
if (-not (Test-Path $helpersDst)) {
    Assert-Pass "T2: --no-copy skips helpers.js"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T2: --no-copy skips helpers.js" "file was unexpectedly copied"
}

$buttonDst = Join-Path $dist2 "components\Button.js"
if (Test-Path $buttonDst) {
    Assert-Pass "T2: --no-copy still transpiles Button.jsx"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T2: --no-copy still transpiles Button.jsx" "Button.js missing"
}

Remove-Dir $dist2

# ===========================================================================
# Test 3: --pragma h  (alternate pragma in batch)
# ===========================================================================
$dist3 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist3"
Remove-Dir $dist3

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist3 --pragma h --no-copy 2>&1 | Out-Null

$btnOut = (Get-Content (Join-Path $dist3 "components\Button.js") -Raw `
           -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Replace("`r`n","`n").TrimEnd()
if ($btnOut -match "^h\(") {
    Assert-Pass "T3: --pragma h produces h(...)"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T3: --pragma h produces h(...)" "output does not start with h("
}

Remove-Dir $dist3

# ===========================================================================
# Test 4: --jsx-runtime automatic
# ===========================================================================
$dist4 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist4"
Remove-Dir $dist4

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist4 --jsx-runtime automatic --no-copy 2>&1 | Out-Null

$btnOut4 = (Get-Content (Join-Path $dist4 "components\Button.js") -Raw `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Replace("`r`n","`n").TrimEnd()
if ($btnOut4 -match "react/jsx-runtime") {
    Assert-Pass "T4: --jsx-runtime automatic injects auto-import"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T4: --jsx-runtime automatic injects auto-import" "auto-import missing"
}

Remove-Dir $dist4

# ===========================================================================
# Test 5: --verbose  (output lines contain ->)
# ===========================================================================
$dist5 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist5"
Remove-Dir $dist5

$verbOut = (& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist5 --verbose --no-copy 2>&1 | Out-String)
if ($verbOut -match "->") {
    Assert-Pass "T5: --verbose prints file paths"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T5: --verbose prints file paths" "no '->' found in output"
}

Remove-Dir $dist5

# ===========================================================================
# Test 6: --threads 1  (single-threaded path, same output)
# ===========================================================================
$dist6 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist6"
Remove-Dir $dist6

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist6 --threads 1 2>&1 | Out-Null

Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "components\Button.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist6  "components\Button.js") `
             "T6: --threads 1 Button.js correct"

Compare-File (Join-Path $ExpDir "utils\helpers.js") `
             (Join-Path $dist6  "utils\helpers.js") `
             "T6: --threads 1 helpers.js copied"

Remove-Dir $dist6

# ===========================================================================
# Test 7: Explicit file list with --out-dir
# ===========================================================================
$dist7 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist7"
Remove-Dir $dist7

$btnSrc  = Join-Path $SrcDir "components\Button.jsx"
$iconSrc = Join-Path $SrcDir "components\Icon.jsx"
& $Binary $btnSrc $iconSrc --out-dir $dist7 2>&1 | Out-Null

# With explicit files, output goes under dist7 relative to the common parent
# (components/ in this case); the binary uses the parent of the first file
# as srcDir, so output will be dist7/Button.js and dist7/Icon.js
$btnFile  = Join-Path $dist7 "Button.js"
$iconFile = Join-Path $dist7 "Icon.js"

if ((Test-Path $btnFile) -and (Test-Path $iconFile)) {
    Assert-Pass "T7: explicit file list creates both outputs"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T7: explicit file list creates both outputs" `
        "missing: $(if (-not (Test-Path $btnFile)) { 'Button.js ' }) $(if (-not (Test-Path $iconFile)) { 'Icon.js' })"
}

Remove-Dir $dist7

# ===========================================================================
# Test 8: Error isolation — bad file does not kill the batch
# ===========================================================================
$dist8    = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist8"
$badSrc   = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "bad_src"
Remove-Dir $dist8
Remove-Dir $badSrc
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $badSrc | Out-Null

# good file
Copy-Item (Join-Path $SrcDir "components\Button.jsx") (Join-Path $badSrc "Good.jsx")
# bad file (parse error)
Set-Content (Join-Path $badSrc "Bad.jsx") "export default function Bad() { return <div class=broken />; }"

$exitBad = 0
& $Binary $badSrc --out-dir $dist8 2>&1 | Out-Null
$exitBad = $LASTEXITCODE

if ($exitBad -ne 0) {
    Assert-Pass "T8: batch exits non-zero when a file has errors"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T8: batch exits non-zero when a file has errors" "expected exit 1"
}

if (Test-Path (Join-Path $dist8 "Good.js")) {
    Assert-Pass "T8: good file still transpiled despite bad file"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T8: good file still transpiled despite bad file" "Good.js missing"
}

Remove-Dir $dist8
Remove-Dir $badSrc

# ===========================================================================
# Test 9: Non-existent source directory reports error
# ===========================================================================
$dist9 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist9"
Remove-Dir $dist9

$errOut = (& $Binary (Join-Path $Stage3Dir "no_such_dir") --out-dir $dist9 2>&1 | Out-String)
$exit9  = $LASTEXITCODE

if ($exit9 -ne 0) {
    Assert-Pass "T9: non-existent src dir exits non-zero"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T9: non-existent src dir exits non-zero" "unexpected exit 0"
}

Remove-Dir $dist9

# ===========================================================================
# Test 10: --jsx-pragma alias works the same as --pragma
# ===========================================================================
$dist10 = Join-Path $Stage3Dir "dist10"
Remove-Dir $dist10

& $Binary $SrcDir --out-dir $dist10 --jsx-pragma h --no-copy 2>&1 | Out-Null

$btnOut10 = (Get-Content (Join-Path $dist10 "components\Button.js") -Raw `
             -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Replace("`r`n","`n").TrimEnd()
if ($btnOut10 -match "^h\(") {
    Assert-Pass "T10: --jsx-pragma alias works"
} else {
    Assert-Fail "T10: --jsx-pragma alias works" "output does not start with h("
}

Remove-Dir $dist10

# ===========================================================================
# Summary
# ===========================================================================
Write-Host ""
Cyan "Results: "; Nl
Green  "  $pass passed"; Nl
if ($fail -gt 0) { Red "  $fail failed"; Nl }
Write-Host ""

if ($fail -gt 0) { exit 1 } else { exit 0 }

arguments.content:
# Yggdrasil

A JSX-to-JavaScript transpiler written in C++17.  
Yggdrasil parses JSX source files and emits standard JavaScript — the same transformation Babel performs with `@babel/plugin-transform-react-jsx`.

It operates in three modes:
- **Single-file** — transpile one `.jsx` to stdout or a file
- **Batch** — transpile an entire source directory tree in parallel
- **Watch** — monitor the source tree and re-transpile on every save

---

## Features

### Stage 1 — Core JSX transpilation
- Self-closing, opening/closing, and nested JSX elements
- Component tags (uppercase), member-expression tags (`Foo.Bar`)
- String, expression, boolean, and spread (`{...obj}`) attributes
- JSX fragments (`<>...</>`)
- Text children, expression children (`{expr}`), and mapped children
- Full JavaScript: `const`/`let`/`var`, arrow functions, destructuring params, `async`/`await`, template literals, spread, ternary, logical operators, `import`/`export` (default, named, namespace, side-effect)
- Diagnostic output with `file:line:col` format

### Stage 2 — Solid Tool extensions
- **Configurable JSX pragma** via `--pragma`: `react` (default), `h`, `jsx`, `auto`
- **React 17 auto-import** (`--pragma auto` / `--jsx-runtime automatic`): prepends `import { jsx as _jsx, ... } from 'react/jsx-runtime'`
- **Dev mode** (`--dev`): injects `__source` and `__self` props
- **Namespace tags**: `<svg:circle />` → `"svg:circle"`
- **JSX comments**: `{/* ... */}` silently dropped
- **Spread children**: `{...items}` in JSX children
- **Hyphenated attributes**: `data-*`, `aria-*` → quoted keys (`"data-x": val`)
- **Multi-error recovery** (`--recover`): collects up to 20 errors, reports all
- **Per-fixture CLI flags**: `.flags` files for the test runner

### Stage 3 — Directory CLI & Batch Transpiler
- **Recursive directory scan** — mirrors `src/` tree into `dist/` with `std::filesystem`
- **Parallel transpilation** — custom thread pool (`std::thread` + mutex/condition_variable), defaults to `hardware_concurrency` threads
- **Passthrough copy** — plain `.js` files copied untouched; skipped with `--no-copy`
- **Watch mode** — re-transpiles changed files on save:
  - Windows: `ReadDirectoryChangesW` (low-latency, native)
  - Other platforms: configurable polling loop (default 500 ms)
- **Error isolation** — one bad file never kills the batch; errors aggregated and reported at the end
- **`--jsx-pragma` / `--jsx-runtime` aliases** for toolchain compatibility
- **`--verbose`** — prints `src/Foo.jsx  ->  dist/Foo.js` for every file
- **`--threads N`** — explicit worker count

---

## Building

### Requirements
- `clang++` with C++17 support
- `make` (GNU Make)
- PowerShell 5.1+ (Windows) or bash (Unix/macOS)

### Build

```sh
# Default
make

# Optimised release
make release

# Debug with ASan/UBSan
make debug

# Clean
make clean
```

Binary: `bin/yggdrasil` (Unix) or `bin\yggdrasil.exe` (Windows).

---

## Usage

```
Usage:
  yggdrasil [options] <input.jsx>                   single file
  yggdrasil [options] --out-dir <dir> <files...>    explicit batch
  yggdrasil [options] <srcDir> --out-dir <dir>      directory batch

Options:
  -o <file>                  Output file (single-file mode)
  --out-dir <dir>            Output directory
  --pragma <name>            JSX pragma: react (default), h, jsx, auto
  --jsx-pragma <name>        Alias for --pragma
  --jsx-runtime <mode>       classic (default) | automatic
  --dev                      Emit __source/__self dev props
  --no-copy                  Skip .js passthrough in batch mode
  --verbose                  Print each file processed
  --watch                    Re-transpile on file changes
  --threads <n>              Worker thread count
  --recover                  Collect multiple errors before stopping
  -h, --help                 Show this help
```

### Examples

```sh
# Single file to stdout
yggdrasil App.jsx

# Single file to output
yggdrasil App.jsx -o App.js

# Directory batch
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/

# Directory batch — Preact pragma, skip .js copy, verbose
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --jsx-pragma h --no-copy --verbose

# Watch mode (re-transpile on save)
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --watch

# React 17 automatic runtime
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --jsx-runtime automatic

# Explicit files
yggdrasil --out-dir dist/ src/Button.jsx src/Icon.jsx

# Parallel with 4 threads
yggdrasil src/ --out-dir dist/ --threads 4

# Multi-error recovery
yggdrasil --recover broken.jsx
```

---

## JSX Pragma Modes

| Flag | Pragma call | Fragment | Use case |
|------|-------------|----------|----------|
| `--pragma react` | `React.createElement` | `React.Fragment` | Classic React (default) |
| `--pragma h` | `h` | `Fragment` | Preact, hyperscript |
| `--pragma jsx` | `_jsx` | `_Fragment` | Custom alias |
| `--pragma auto` | `_jsx` | `_Fragment` | React 17+ with auto-import |

`--jsx-runtime automatic` is equivalent to `--pragma auto` and prepends:
```js
import { jsx as _jsx, jsxs as _jsxs, Fragment as _Fragment } from "react/jsx-runtime";
```

## Running Tests

```sh

make test

# Stage 3 batch/directory tests

# Filter fixture tests
```

### Fixture conventions

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `*.jsx` | Input source |
| `*.expected.js` | Expected transpiled output |
| `*.expected_exit` | Expected exit code (error tests) |
| `*.flags` | Extra CLI flags for that fixture |

## Architecture

```
include/
  token.h        TokenKind enum + Token struct
  lexer.h        Self-managing mode-stack lexer (JS / JSXTag / JSXChildren)
  ast.h          Flat Node struct + NodeKind enum
  parser.h       Recursive-descent parser with JSX grammar + error recovery
  codegen.h      CodeGen + CodeGenOptions (pragma, dev, indent)
  diagnostics.h  LexError / ParseError / CodeGenError + ErrorCollector
  batch.h        BatchEngine: recursive scan, parallel transpile/copy
  threadpool.h   Fixed-size thread pool (std::thread + condition_variable)
  watcher.h      File watcher (ReadDirectoryChangesW / polling)

src/
  lexer.cpp      Context-aware tokeniser — self-pushes/pops JSX modes
  parser.cpp     Full JS + JSX parser; optional multi-error recovery
  codegen.cpp    AST walker; lowers JSX to configurable pragma calls
  diagnostics.cpp  ErrorCollector::dump()
  batch.cpp      BatchEngine::run() + processFile()
  threadpool.cpp ThreadPool worker loop
  watcher.cpp    watchWindows() + watchPolling()
  main.cpp       CLI: single-file, batch, directory, watch modes

tests/
  fixtures/      48 unit fixtures (*.jsx + *.expected.js|*.expected_exit|*.flags)
  stage3/
    src/         Sample directory tree (components/, pages/, utils/)
    expected/    Pre-computed expected outputs for batch comparison
  runner/
    run_tests.ps1        Stage 1+2 fixture runner
    run_stage3_tests.ps1 Stage 3 batch/directory tests (17 scenarios)
```

### Key design decisions

**Self-managing lexer mode stack** — the lexer tracks JSX context internally (`JSXTag` / `JSXChildren` / `JS`), pushed/popped as it emits specific tokens. The parser never needs to call `pushMode`/`popMode`.

**Flat AST node** — all node kinds share one `Node` struct. Avoids virtual dispatch and header pollution.

**Parallel batch with error isolation** — each file runs in its own thread-pool task. A `std::mutex` guards the shared `BatchResult`. One failing file increments `failed` but other tasks continue uninterrupted.

**Watch mode strategy** — on Windows, `ReadDirectoryChangesW` with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` gives sub-second latency with zero CPU spin. On other platforms, a polling loop with configurable interval is used. The watcher calls `BatchEngine::processFile()` directly — same code path as batch.

**Brace-depth tracking** — to correctly pop back from `{expr}` inside JSX, the lexer maintains a stack of brace depths recorded at each JS-inside-JSX entry point.

## Supported JSX Grammar

```
JSXElement      ::= '<' JSXTagName JSXAttribute* ('/>' | '>' JSXChild* JSXClosingTag)
JSXFragment     ::= '<>' JSXChild* '</>'
JSXTagName      ::= Identifier ('.' Identifier)* | Identifier ':' Identifier
JSXChild        ::= JSXText | JSXExprContainer | JSXElement | JSXFragment
JSXExprContainer::= '{' ('...' Expr | Expr | /* comment */) '}'
JSXAttribute    ::= JSXSpread | JSXAttrName ('=' JSXAttrValue)?
JSXSpread       ::= '{' '...' Expr '}'
JSXAttrName     ::= Identifier ('-' Identifier)*    (data-*, aria-*)
JSXAttrValue    ::= JSXString | JSXExprContainer
```

---

## What Yggdrasil Does NOT Do

- Parse or resolve `import`/`export` module paths
- Touch `node_modules`
- Build dependency graphs or bundle files
- Tree-shake, concatenate, or minify
- Handle CSS, assets, or non-JS/JSX files
- Emit source maps
